title: Advance Fee Scam
description: You are asked to pay a fee before receiving money. Legitimate services never require you to send money first to receive a transfer.
advice: STOP immediately. Never send money to receive money. This is one of the most common scams targeting foreigners in Japan.
examples: You won a prize, pay the processing fee to claim it
Pay a small fee to unlock your inheritance
Transfer fee required before your loan is approved

title: Cryptocurrency Payment Scam
description: Someone is asking you to send money via cryptocurrency. Scammers prefer crypto because transactions are irreversible and hard to trace.
advice: Legitimate businesses and government agencies NEVER request payment in cryptocurrency. If someone insists on crypto payment, it is almost certainly a scam.
examples: Send Bitcoin to this wallet address
Convert your money to USDT and transfer
Use this crypto exchange to send payment

title: Romance Scam
description: Someone you met online (LINE, WhatsApp, dating apps, social media) is asking you to send money. This is extremely common in Japan, targeting both foreigners and Japanese.
advice: Never send money to someone you haven't met in person. Scammers build emotional connections over weeks or months before asking for money. Report to police (Cybercrime Division).
examples: My partner I met on Tinder needs money for an emergency
Someone on LINE asked me to invest together
A person on WhatsApp says they're stuck abroad and need money

title: Immigration Authority Scam
description: Someone claiming to be from Japanese Immigration (Nyukan) is asking you to send money. The Immigration Bureau NEVER contacts people by phone/email to demand payment.
advice: Hang up immediately. The real Immigration Services Agency of Japan will send official letters by mail. If concerned, visit your local immigration office in person.
examples: Immigration says you must pay a fine immediately
Your visa will be cancelled unless you pay now
You'll be deported if you don't send money

title: Lottery/Prize Scam
description: You received a message saying you won a lottery or prize you never entered. They'll ask for a 'processing fee' or your bank details.
advice: You cannot win a lottery you never entered. Delete the message immediately. Never share bank account details with unknown parties.
examples: Congratulations! You won the Japan International Lottery
You've been selected as a lucky winner, pay the fee to claim
Your email was randomly selected for a cash prize

title: Investment Scam
description: Someone is promising guaranteed high returns on an investment. No legitimate investment guarantees profits. This is especially common on LINE and social media in Japan.
advice: No investment is risk-free or guaranteed. Check if the company is registered with Japan's FSA (Financial Services Agency). Report to the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission.
examples: Invest in this forex fund for guaranteed 30% monthly returns
Double your money in 30 days with this crypto trading bot
Exclusive investment opportunity only for foreigners in Japan

title: Bank Phishing Scam
description: You received an email or SMS that looks like it's from your bank, asking you to click a link or verify your account. Japanese banks are frequently impersonated.
advice: Never click links in emails/SMS from your bank. Always go directly to your bank's official website or app. Call your bank's official number if concerned.
examples: Your Yucho account has been suspended, click here to verify
SBI security alert: unusual activity detected
Confirm your identity to avoid account closure

title: Unlicensed Money Transfer
description: Using unlicensed money transfer services (underground banking) is illegal in Japan. You could lose your money AND face criminal charges.
advice: Only use services licensed by Japan's FSA (Financial Services Agency). Check the FSA registry. Using unlicensed services can result in fines and deportation.
examples: My friend can send money to your country cheaper than Wise
Use this cash transfer network, no fees
This informal service has better rates than banks

title: Tech Support Scam
description: Someone claims your computer has a virus and asks you to install remote access software or pay for 'repairs'. They may ask for payment via convenience store gift cards or wire transfer.
advice: Microsoft, Apple, and other companies never make unsolicited calls about viruses. Hang up. Never install remote access software for strangers. Never buy gift cards as payment.
examples: Microsoft detected a virus on your computer
Pay for tech support with iTunes gift cards
Install TeamViewer so we can fix your computer

title: Recognized Money Transfer Service
description: This appears to be a recognized, licensed money transfer service. However, always verify you're on the official website and not a phishing site.
advice: This service is generally safe to use. Always access through official websites/apps. Compare fees and rates before sending. Keep transaction receipts.
